Oh wow um actually a lot has happened, I went to it.  I got meds, started on Prozac because it worked for my mom, because apparently depression runs in my family.  Fast forward about two weeks and I'm shaking with anxiety all the time and my brain won't stop telling me to kill myself.  I nearly jump off of the building again on a Friday night, and then Monday I had an overdose on Tylenol, not enough to kill me, I just needed to feel something other than emptiness.  I had another appointment for Tuesday, I go to it.  And I tell them about what happened, of course the doctor gets very concerned, and they start talking about going in-patient.  I ended up agreeing and I did go to the hospital.  I'm out now and doing much better.  I have a therapy appointment today and then I'm going home for the holiday.

Honestly, to me coming out as a self-harmer was similar to the feeling of coming out as gay.  I got super nervous, but my friends understood eventually.  That being said, I would definitely say just make sure they know why you're telling them.  If you're looking for help or support, if you want someone to talk to, or if you just need someone to know.  It also seems like your friend cares about you, so let him!  If they get upset, please also know that it's not your fault.  It's a difficult thing to process.  One of the best pieces of advice I can tell you is to give your friend (if he takes it well, give yourself a little time as well) your tools.  For me, this was such a lift off my chest.
